note_tweet.text:
The US government should be terrified about the current state of AI lab security. From our interview with @alexandr_wang releasing on ChinaTalk tomorrow, after I asked him what the US government should do if AI takeoff was really around the corner:

"You need to lock down the labs. The immediate thing you have to do, if you believe we are on this fast takeoff scenario, we're imminently close to AGI occurring is prevent all of our secrets from going over to our adversaries and you need to lock down the security of the lab such that you don't face this espionage risk.

There are a lot of ways you can do that. You can implement it as if there's a government agency that's responsible for lab security among all the labs.  I grew up in Los Alamos, so I'm partial to government labs.

Maybe there's some sort of government lab that sort of serves as a parent organization to some extent to all of the sub-labs.

By definition, that's going to require some slowing of the deployment because, once you deploy this stuff for economic reasons, you're also deploying it to be stolen by our adversaries.

The DoD, the intelligence community and the national security community need to immediately take this incredibly seriously.

But it doesn't take a lot of imagination to realize that powerful AI systems, if they existed, would be a definitive military technology. So much so that nuclear deterrence doesn't even really matter in a world where you have advanced AI systems. 

They can do superhuman hacking, you have autonomous drone swarms, you have full situational awareness, you can develop biological weapons."
